text.p: Giorgio Garuzzo, vice-chairman of troubled information and technology group Olivetti, has resigned from the Italian company for personal reasons, chairman Antonio Tesone said.
At the annual shareholders' meeting in Ivrea, Olivetti's home town, Tesone read out a letter from Garuzzo sent in May in which he announced his resignation effective from the shareholders' meeting.
Garuzzo, a former senior executive at Italian industrial giant Fiat, resigned for reasons of personal commitments.
In the letter, he said he was sorry to leave Olivetti but added: "I am convinced that Olivetti still has a huge potential to show."
He was former chief operating officer at Fiat Auto and left under a cloud in February 1996 as part of a shake-up of Fiat top management.
